sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:35

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:35:1
items.html:
The light begins to come into Keter, and all the nine lights are included in it: In order to understand the words of the ARI here, one must remember well, with clear understanding, all his words at the beginning of the part, from item 1 to item 15, and also what we explained there, for it is impossible to repeat all that length here. We shall mention here in brief the main points.
And see first the order of the ascents of the Sefirot to the Emanator after their departure from the first expansion, which was explained (in Part 4, Chapter 4, item 6). And the essence of all the above is that the coupling by striking that was made in the first Partzuf of AK was on a screen corrected in the vessel of Malchut, which stood in the greatness of the coarseness, that is, the coarseness of phase four. Therefore that Malchut raised the greatest reflected light, that is, up to the level of Keter, and this reflected light rose and clothed the upper light from below upward, and these ten Sefirot are called the ten Sefirot of the Rosh. And it is the law of Malchut and of the reflected light that, in the same measure in which it clothes from below upward, it turns back and reverses and widens the vessel of Malchut from above downward, from her and within her, down to that Malchut of Malchut, and descends and clothes there with the whole measure of the level of the direct light that it clothes in the Rosh. And this clothing is called the first expansion of AK, and it is likewise called the ten Sefirot of the Guf. And the Malchut of the Rosh is called Peh, and Malchut of Malchut, which is the Malchut of the Guf, is called Tabur.
And since in the Malchut of the Rosh there is as yet no restraint discernible in practice, the surrounding light and the inner light therefore illuminate there equally. But when the light expanded from there to the ten Sefirot of the Guf, down to the Tabur, which is the Malchut of the Guf, the screen of the Tabur stopped the direct light and did not let it expand below the Tabur. That is, that direct light which belongs to the first nine Sefirot, which is called inner light, clothed in the nine Sefirot of the Guf down to the Tabur; and that direct light which belongs to Malchut could not enter and clothe in its place, which is below the Tabur, because of the screen that is there, and it remained outside the Partzuf in the secret of surrounding light.
Therefore a striking and a clash occur between the surrounding light and the inner light at this boundary, which is called the screen of the Tabur.
For the surrounding light, too, wished to descend and clothe in its place like the inner light, since in the Rosh both of them illuminated equally, as above. Therefore the surrounding light overcomes and refines the screen of its coarseness, so that the detaining force in it will vanish from it and the surrounding light will be able to clothe as well. And understand this well, for this is the secret of the whole matter of the refinement of the screen in each and every Partzuf. For since in every Rosh no restraint upon the surrounding light is discernible, it therefore wishes to clothe in the Guf as well, and therefore it refines the coarseness in the screen, that is, the aspect of detaining in it, for the measure of coarseness in the screen is the measure of its detaining, and in it they are one and the same matter.
And indeed, the surrounding light refined all the coarseness present in the screen at once, and they brought it to the Emanator, that is, to the Peh of the Rosh, where it has no restraint, as above. This means that the screen was refined of all the coarseness of the Guf, and nothing remained in it but the aspect of the root within it, which is the aspect of the screen of the Malchut of the Rosh; for this is what is called that it rose to the Peh, since equivalence of form makes spiritual things one.
However, since there are four degrees in the coarseness, it is necessary that the screen which had in it the aspect of the coarseness of phase four, and which was refined entirely, necessarily passed through those four degrees one after the other. Also, the upper light does not cease illuminating even for a moment; it is simply not discerned in the worlds unless there is a fitting receiver to receive His light. Therefore we discern that the upper light couples with the screen on its way through the four degrees that lie from phase four until complete refinement, and brings out along its way four levels of light according to the measure of coarseness in which the screen stands; for as long as there is still in it some measure of coarseness fit for coupling, the upper light still connects and clothes in it. And understand this well.
And likewise, when the level departs — even though it certainly departs at once — we nevertheless discern in it that it makes four stops along its way. For example, when it refines from phase four to phase three, the level of Keter vanishes from the Partzuf; and since there are five degrees — KHB, ZA and Malchut — in the level of Keter, we discern in the order of its departure that it makes four stops along its way. For first the Keter of that level vanishes and only the nine lower Sefirot remain there, and then Hochma has risen to the place of Keter, and Bina to the place of Hochma, and so on until Malchut to the place of ZA. And afterwards Hochma vanishes from the level, and then Bina rises to the place of Keter, and ZA to the place of Hochma, and Malchut to the place of Bina. And afterwards Bina, too, vanishes from the level, and ZA rises to the place of Keter and Malchut to the place of Hochma. And afterwards ZA, too, vanishes from the level, and Malchut rises to the place of Keter. And finally Malchut, too, vanishes from the level, and then the whole level of Keter has departed from the Partzuf. Thus even in a single level we discern that it makes four stops in the midst of its departure. However, one must understand that the matter of couplings with the screen does not apply during the departure of a single level, since there is no renewal of form in the coarseness at the time of the departure; and before the screen arrives at the coarseness of phase three, there is nothing to discern there but the refinement of a single phase, and that refinement pushes and removes the reflected light, since it is then unfit for coupling, being occupied with its own refinement from that measure.
It is also known that the above screen of the Tabur of the first expansion, which refined and arrived at the Peh, was included in all the records of the ten Sefirot of the Guf, except for phase four, who left no record of bestowal of her own, and nothing remained of her but a record of clothing, as written in the Inner Light, page 297, the passage beginning “that refines,” study there well the whole of that passage, for all of it is needed here. And it was explained there that we reckon primarily with the highest of them, which is phase three, that draws the level of Hochma; but since there is there also the aspect of the record of phase four of clothing, called the aspect of the male of the vessel of Keter, which on the one hand is immeasurably higher than phase three, being of the aspect of the level of Keter — yet since it has nothing of the aspect of the coarseness of drawing, it must therefore join with the aspect of the female, which means with the aspect of the coarseness of drawing, which is the record of phase three, in which there is also the aspect of drawing, as was explained there at length, and study it there.
And now let us come to the actual explanation of the words of the ARI, for he says, “first the light begins to come into Keter, and all the nine lights are included in it.” And there are two things to consider here. The first: why the order here is reversed from what it was in the first expansion, for there the light began to come into Malchut first, and here it began to expand into Keter first. And the second: why in the first expansion the illuminations each came to the vessel that belongs to it, while here they all came together into a single vessel, that of Keter.
However, if we understand whence these vessels came here, the two above questions will be explained to us plainly. And one must know that although the ARI speaks briefly and says that the lights expanded back into the empty vessels after the lights had departed from within them — which implies that what is spoken of here is only the first Partzuf, in which the departure occurred — nevertheless it is not so. Rather, there is here a matter of a distinct Partzuf, entirely separate from the first Partzuf. For the first Partzuf is called the Partzuf Galgalta of AK, and this second expansion is called the Partzuf AB of AK, and it is considered an offspring and a son of the first Partzuf, since from its coupling this second expansion emerged and was born.
And the ARI has already explained to us the order of this coupling above, page 297, from item 9 to item 15, and they were well explained in the Inner Light there. There is no need to repeat the matter; but one must understand in general that the whole matter of the departure of the lights and of the empty vessels that remained, spoken of in the first Partzuf, all of this already belongs to the second Partzuf. For there is no absence in spirituality, and the whole matter of disparity of form that is discerned in spiritual things means an addition of form, and not an absence or an exchange whatsoever. Therefore all those empty vessels spoken of in the first Partzuf are themselves the vessels of this second expansion, and into them the lights came and expanded back a second time.
Therefore, after the couplings were made on the screen that includes the two records mentioned in the words of the ARI above — which are the record of phase four, called male, and the record of phase three, called female — these two levels expanded into the vessel of Keter, which had remained empty since the time of the first expansion, and in those two levels this whole second expansion is included in its entirety. For just as in the first expansion all the levels were included in the level of Keter, and all four levels — HB and ZON — emerged through the refinement of the screen of the coarseness of phase four, which is the level of Keter, so exactly here, all the ten Sefirot are included in the first level of male and female that emerged inside the vessel of Keter. For afterwards this screen of phase four and phase three refined, and the male and female emerged into the vessel of Hochma, and so on in this manner, exactly as it was in the order of the first expansion, as is written before us.
And with this you will plainly understand that it was impossible for the level of phase three and phase four, which are close to the degree of Keter (as above, page 297, item 9), to clothe in the vessel of Hochma, which is much smaller than they. And likewise they have no place to clothe in the levels HB and ZON, for each and every Sefira of those ten Sefirot of the male and female of Keter is of equal level, that is, each of them is close to the level of Keter; and how could any one of them clothe in the remaining, lower levels of HB, ZA and Malchut.

items.html: Lo Mati [not reaching], that the light that reaches Keter went out from there again. For the screen of phase four of the male refined to phase three, and the screen of phase three of the female to phase two, and because of this the two levels of the male and female of Keter departed. And this is what he says, that the light that reaches Keter went out from there again. And this matter of refinement that befell the male and female of Keter is likewise by reason of the clash and striking of the surrounding light and the inner light, as in the first expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:35:3
items.html: The other nine lights remained in Keter. That is, that the above coarseness of phase two remained in it, and the coupling that emerges on this coarseness draws the level of Bina, and Bina includes within her the level of ZA and Malchut, which are eight lights. Phase three of the male of Keter also remained; thus nine lights remained in the vessel of Keter after the refinement of its own phase.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:35:4
items.html:
Lo Mati in Keter, etc., then Keter draws to Hochma, face to face, the nine lights. You already know that these vessels of the second expansion are those same empty vessels that remained after the first expansion. It was also explained above, in the words of the ARI, page 311, item 26, the order of the formation of these vessels: that first Malchut was made, since she was emptied of her light first; and afterwards, when the vessel of ZA was emptied of its light, the vessel of ZA was made; and afterwards, when the vessel of Bina was emptied, the vessel of Bina was made, and so forth. And the reason for this is that the vessels were made of the coarse light that remained below and did not rise and depart together with the direct light, as the ARI wrote above (Part 4, Chapter 2, item 7). Therefore each and every vessel was made with the departure of the light from within it, for then the coarse light remained below and became a vessel.
And you find that the vessels were arranged, from the time of their formation, one above the other: first Malchut, and above her ZA, and above it Bina, up to the vessel of Keter above them all. And by this you will know that here too, in the second expansion, even before the lights expanded, the vessels are already arranged and stand from above downward, Keter at the head of them all and Malchut at the end, that is, just as they emerged in the first expansion. Therefore, when the lights expanded and emerged from the above coupling of the level of Keter and Hochma, all of whose ten Sefirot were of equal level, close to Keter, as above, they found ready and standing for them the vessel of Keter that suits them.
And now, at the time of Lo Mati in Keter — which means that phase four of the male of Keter and phase three of the Nukva of Keter refined, so that the level of Keter of the male and the level of Hochma of the Nukva departed — it follows from this that all these ten Sefirot of male and female lost the level of Keter in them, and the ten Sefirot of the male diminished to the level of Hochma, and the ten Sefirot of the female diminished to the level of Bina. And this level no longer belongs at all to Keter, but to the vessel of Hochma. Therefore Keter bestowed them to the vessel of Hochma, as the ARI says.
But one must understand how the lights are drawn from the vessel of Keter to the vessel of Hochma, for there is a very great distance between these vessels: the vessel of Keter is in the coarseness of phase four, and the vessel of Hochma is in the coarseness of phase three, and it is known that disparity of form is what separates and distances spiritual things. If so, how do they touch one another, that they may bestow one to the other? And one must not err and say that the vessel of Keter refined to phase three and therefore became equal with the vessel of Hochma, for it is known that no refinement applies to the vessels at all, and the whole matter of refinement that is spoken of is understood only with respect to the screen in the vessels, and not to the vessels themselves.
However, one must remember what the ARI explained above, page 304, item 15, and in the Inner Light, page 305, the passage beginning “and then the vessel turned its face.” It was explained there that when the light departs from the vessel, the vessel turns its face downward and its posterior upward, and the face of the vessel becomes posterior and the posterior becomes face; study it there well, the matter with its reason. And here, after the light belonging to the vessel of Keter departed — for phase four of the male and phase three of the female refined, and the coupling was made on phase three of the male and phase two of the female — then the vessel of Keter turns its face downward, so that its great coarseness, which had been all its face and its importance, now becomes the most inferior aspect, and the posterior, that is, the refined side in it, becomes the most important. Study it there. And with this you will understand that the vessel of Keter, after it turned its posterior upward, is found to be equal with the vessel of Hochma. For all the disparity of form that was in the vessel of Keter is its great coarseness of phase four and phase three, since this is its entire superiority over the vessel of Hochma; and now all this coarseness has already been annulled from it because of the turning of its face downward, as above. Therefore it is now discerned as being in equivalence of form with Hochma.
And this is what he says, “and then Keter draws to Hochma, face to face, the nine lights,” for he hints thereby that because of the departure of the light of Keter, the vessel of Keter turned its face downward, and therefore it is found standing with the vessel of Hochma face to face; for now the face of Keter, too, is phase two and phase three, that is, that same refined side which was previously the aspect of the posterior of Keter, and it is exactly equal with the face of Hochma. Therefore it can bestow the light to Hochma, since they are in equivalence of form with one another. And this is the reason for the rule the ARI gives us further on, that every giving of lights is always in the aspect of face to face.
And the matter of these nine lights that Hochma received from Keter has already been explained above: they are the remainder of the coarseness that remained of the male of Keter after its refinement, which is phase three, and which is the aspect of the record of Hochma of the first expansion that was included in the male of Keter (as above in the Inner Light, page 294, the passage beginning “and know that their essence,” study it there well). And this is one light. She also received the remainder of the coarseness of the female of Keter, which is phase two and the level of Bina, in which the two levels of ZA and of Malchut are included, which are together eight lights; and with phase three of the male, they are nine lights.

items.html:
Hochma turned her face after she received the nine lights, and illuminates to Bina. Meaning the turning of the face of the male of Hochma alone, and not of the aspect of the female of Hochma. For the turning of the face means the refinement of the coarseness and the departure of the light from there, for then the vessel turns its face downward, as above in the words of the ARI, page 304, item 15. Therefore, after Hochma received her nine lights from Keter, which are the male and female of the vessel of Hochma, as above in the adjacent item, then the screen of the coarseness of phase three of the male refined to the aspect of the coarseness of phase two, and the vessel of the male is found turning its face downward and its posterior upward, which means that the importance of the aspect of the greatness of its coarseness is annulled (as above, page 305, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “and then the vessel,” study it there well). And then this remainder of the male of Hochma is bestowed to the vessel of Bina. And this is what he says, Hochma turned her face after she received the nine lights and illuminates to Bina, that is, to the aspect of the male of the vessel of Bina, as above.
However, with respect to the aspect of the male of the vessel of Keter, the ARI did not explain above any refinement, but included it together with the female of Keter in a single refinement. And the reason is that the male of Keter has in it nothing at all of the aspect of the coarseness of drawing, but only of the aspect of clothing, as above; and in the aspect of clothing, by its own attribution alone, the matter of refinement does not apply to it, since it has no coarseness at all, but is included and joined with the coarseness of the female, as above (in the Inner Light, page 298, the passage beginning “however there is here”). Therefore the matter of its refinement, too, comes together with the refinement of the screen of the female, and the ARI therefore included them in a single refinement.
But the male of the vessel of Hochma, which is the aspect of the record of the light of Hochma that remained from the first expansion, as in the adjacent item, has in it also the aspect of the coarseness of drawing, and it must therefore refine before the female refines, for the measure of its coarseness is greater, since it is phase three and the female is phase two, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:35:6
items.html: An illumination alone, but she does not yet give her the seven lights. That is, that it gives only one light, that of the male of the vessel of Bina, for its time has now come to refine, and it gives its remainder to Bina. But the time of the female has not yet come to refine, and therefore she does not yet give the seven lights that belong to the female of Bina, as was explained in the adjacent item.
